# Factory-wide settings: names, shape, layers, fields and metadata, across the nine sources and the wider field (2026)

Research date: 2026-10-23. Read from the nine sources' cached docs (`bun run sources`, fetched 2026-10-22 22:17 UTC into `.generated/sources/`) and their published packages, then from the official docs and source code of the wider field. Every count is by meaning: a source counts only when it uses the word or shape for app-wide settings, not for an HTTP option or one call's arguments. The raw word counts from `bun run terms` are kept as context; every word appears in all nine, so they do not decide.

The concept: factory settings, the choices that hold for the whole factory, such as which bridge to use, saved in the database through a setup step rather than in env vars ([ADR 0005](../adr/0005-agents-run-in-cli-harnesses-through-a-bridge.md), [ADR 0007](../adr/0007-one-local-postgres-and-no-sync-engine-yet.md)). Out of scope: the settings one Claude run was launched with (model, `--settings`, MCP config, `--add-dir`), the deferred record of how one run was launched; overlaps are noted where found.

Labels: [Docs] official documentation · [Types] a published `.d.ts` or package source · [Source] source code at the commit or tag named · [Inferred] a conclusion drawn from what was read, not stated by the source.

Singular or plural. No source defines a record type named `Setting`. Across the eight published packages every type for a group of choices is plural `...Settings` (`Settings`, `ResolvedSettings`, `SandboxSettings`, `CallSettings`, `ModelSettings`, `AISettings`, `ProviderSettings`) or the mass noun `Config` (`Config.Info`, `RunConfig`, `AgentControllerConfig`); the one singular type, eve's `AgentModelSetting`, names a single key ("model", "reasoning" or "fast-mode") [Types]. In prose the singular means one key: Claude Code's "Change a setting", "a setting saved in it applies to" [Docs]. So the sources use **settings** for the whole group and **setting** for one key; none stores one row per key under a singular name.

Preferences. In the nine, "preferences" is never a file, a type or a page. It is either macOS's delivery mechanism ("managed preferences that MDM tools deploy for the `ai.opencode.managed` domain", OpenCode; the same in Claude Code and Codex) or a description of what goes in the user layer: Claude Code's scope table says user settings are for "Personal preferences: theme, editor mode, default model, your own permission rules" [Docs]. "Options" names a constructor's or call's arguments (Mastra's "all supported options", the Agent SDK's `Options`), not a stored record.

Tally across the 13: "settings" in code in 8 (Emdash, Superset, Nimbalyst, OpenCode app, Mastra Code, Mastra Factory, T3 Code, opcode), "config" in 6 (Crystal, OpenCode's `opencode.json`, mux, vibe-kanban, AionUi, CloudCLI's `app_config`), "preferences" as a table name in 2 (Crystal, CloudCLI) and as a sub-object or section in 3 (mux `userPreferences`, Mastra Code `preferences`, Emdash's section). The page is "Settings" in all 9 that were checked (Emdash, Superset, Crystal, Nimbalyst, OpenCode, CloudCLI, opcode, mux, vibe-kanban) and assumed so in T3 Code and AionUi; Mastra Code and Mastra Factory have none. None calls it "Preferences".

[Docs] | https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/configuring-project-and-ide-settings.html                                                |

[Docs]                                              | https://manual.raycast.com/settings                                                                                          |

[Docs]    | https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings                                                       |

Tally across the 12 products: the record is plural "settings" in 8 (VS Code, Zed, Cursor's IDE, Letta, Linear, Slack's admin methods, Warp, JetBrains), "config" or "configuration" in 3 (VS Code's API, Cursor's CLI, LangGraph) and "options" in 1 (Agent Framework). None names the whole record `Setting`; the singular is one key (VS Code's "a setting", Linear's AI tool `ReadSetting(id)`), and GitHub's custom properties keep one row per key under the name "property". The page is "Settings" in all 9 that have one, which Apple's guidelines also prescribe; "Preferences" survives only as a per-user page (Slack, Linear's Account > Preferences) and as VS Code's command prefix.

All nine model app-wide choices as one typed document. None keeps them in Postgres; the three that keep any in a database (OpenCode's desktop SQLite, Cloudflare's SQLite, Mastra's storage) keep a typed JSON document in a row, never one row or column per field. Three write one key at a time into a typed document: Codex's `config/value/write`, Claude Code's `/config key=value` and eve's `eve set model` [Docs].

The other six GUIs keep settings in files, as one typed document each: Crystal's `config.json`, Nimbalyst (electron-store, its database holds no settings), Mastra Code, T3 Code (its SQLite has no settings table), mux and vibe-kanban; AionUi keeps a flat dotted-key map in one file. Nimbalyst reads and writes its documents one key at a time through a registry of key, Zod schema and path: "Per-key reads/writes never affect other keys (no spread, no blob merge). Adding a new setting is one line in this file: declare key + Zod schema." [Source]

Two costs show in the migration history. Superset's singleton row, one column per setting, is touched by 39 of its 60 migrations (`telemetry_enabled` was added in migration 0016 and dropped in 0018); Emdash's key-value `app_settings` is touched by 1 of its 47 [Source]. Four store only what differs from the defaults and fill the defaults in on read: Emdash, T3 Code (`stripDefaultServerSettings`), mux and Mastra Factory [Source].

All 12 wider products keep settings as a typed document; key-value appears only for app state (VS Code's `ItemTable`, Zed's `kv_store`) and for open extension points (GitHub custom properties, Linear's `settings: JSONObject`, the Agent Framework's `AdditionalProperties`, LangGraph's `configurable`). Every key-value table found, in the GUIs and the wider field, names its columns `key` and `value`, except CloudCLI's `preference_key` and `preference_value`.

## 3. Scope or layers

| Source            | Layers, lowest precedence first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Merge                                                                                                                                 | Quote                                                                                                                                                                                                | Link                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anomaly OpenCode  | global (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) → project files from the farthest directory to the closest (direct files, then `.opencode/` ones) → system (`/etc/opencode`) → macOS managed preferences. `cli.json` has one global file plus the `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` env | Keys override; "Settings that do not conflict are preserved"; some keys global-only ("Project-level values are ignored" for `update`) | "The package config overrides matching settings from the repository config, which overrides the global config. The system config overrides all of them." [Docs]                                      | https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config/                               |
| Claude Agent SDK  | `SettingSource`: user → project → local; `ResolvedSettingSource` adds `flag` and `managed` on top                                                                                                                                                                               | `resolveSettings()` returns `effective`, per-key `provenance`, and `sources` "low→high precedence"                                    | "Source that contributed an effective setting value. Filesystem sources use the same names as SettingSource; `'managed'` is the policy tier ... `'flag'` is the `--settings` CLI flag tier." [Types] | `sdk.d.ts` (`ResolvedSettingSource`)                              |
| Claude Code       | user (`~/.claude/settings.json`) → shared project (`.claude/settings.json`) → project local (`.claude/settings.local.json`) → command line (`--settings`) → managed                                                                                                             | Higher level wins per key; lists such as `permissions.allow` merge                                                                    | "Settings precedence, highest first: managed settings, command line, project local, shared project, user." [Docs]                                                                                    | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings                          |
| Cloudflare Agents | None: one config per agent instance, `initialState` as the default                                                                                                                                                                                                              | n/a                                                                                                                                   | "Use the `initialState` property to define default values for new agent instances" [Docs]                                                                                                            | https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/runtime/lifecycle/state/ |
| Mastra            | Code config → controller and Session defaults → thread settings                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Narrower wins                                                                                                                         | "These selections are written to thread settings. An agent-type selection takes precedence over the Session's default subagent model." [Docs]                                                        | https://mastra.ai/docs/harness/agent-controller                   |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` env → agent → `Runner`'s `RunConfig` → one `run()` call                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `RunConfig.modelSettings` overrides the agent's; a per-run value overrides the Runner's                                               | "`Runner`‑level settings override conflicting per-agent settings." [Docs]                                                                                                                            | https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models           |
| OpenAI Codex      | built-in defaults → system (`/etc/codex/config.toml`) → cloud-managed defaults → user (`~/.codex/config.toml`) → profile (`~/.codex/<name>.config.toml`) → project (`.codex/config.toml`, closest wins, trusted only) → CLI flags; `requirements.toml` constrains all           | Higher wins per key; managed `requirements.toml` cannot be overridden                                                                 | "Requirements constrain behavior; configuration values provide defaults." [Docs]                                                                                                                     | https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic           |
| Vercel AI SDK     | `globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` → `defaultSettingsMiddleware` → call settings → `prepareCall` / `prepareStep`                                                                                                                                                              | Later replaces earlier                                                                                                                | "The returned object replaces the call settings, so spread the incoming settings and override only the ones you want to change." [Docs]                                                              | https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/agents/configuring-call-options           |
| Vercel eve        | None: the root agent's `agent.ts`, or eve's default when the file is absent                                                                                                                                                                                                     | n/a                                                                                                                                   | "The root `agent.ts` can be omitted when no runtime config is needed. eve then selects its default `agent.ts` source" [Docs]                                                                         | https://eve.dev/docs/agent-config                                 |

The four that layer files (OpenCode, Claude Agent SDK, Claude Code, Codex) share three layers by meaning: **user** (one person on one machine: Claude's and Codex's "user", OpenCode's "global" or "user settings"), **project** (one repository) and **managed** or **system** (an organization or machine admin). Claude Code and its Agent SDK alone add **local** (one person in one shared project), Codex alone adds **profile**, and all four add a one-run layer (Claude Code's `--settings`, the SDK's `flag` tier, Codex's `-c`, OpenCode's env). The narrower layer wins over the broader one in all four; managed wins over everything in three (Claude Code, the Agent SDK, OpenCode), while Codex puts its managed config defaults below the user and enforces policy through `requirements.toml` instead [Docs].

Three keep some app-wide keys out of project files. OpenCode keeps all its UI settings (theme, notifications) user-only: "There is no project-local CLI settings file." Codex ignores `notify`, `otel`, `profile` and provider keys in a project's `.codex/config.toml`, and Claude Code drops the env variables that turn telemetry on from project and local settings [Docs]. Claude Code's `theme` and `preferredNotifChannel`, by contrast, may sit in any file.

OpenCode's source adds layers its docs leave out: a remote `.well-known` config below the global file, and `OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` around the project files [Source, v2.1.3].

Policy or team layers on top appear only where an organization manages the product (VS Code, Cursor, GitHub, Slack). Profiles appear in 3 of the 34 products read (Codex, VS Code, Zed).

- Claude Code telemetry: "The switches that turn off usage metrics and error reports are environment variables, not settings keys" [Docs] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference

Overlap with the deferred run record: `model`, `effortLevel`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `teammateMode` and the hook keys are all settings keys a run is launched with; Claude Code's command-line layer (`--settings`, "for that session only") and the Agent SDK's `flag` tier are exactly what a run record would keep, so a factory default and a run's launch settings can share key names but are different records [Inferred].

Of the 13 products that keep settings in database rows, 11 keep an update time on the row (Emdash, Crystal, OpenCode, Mastra, Mastra Factory, CloudCLI, opcode, LangGraph, Linear, GitHub, Letta's archived server); the two that do not are Superset's singleton row and Cloudflare's `think_config`. File documents keep none and carry a schema reference or a version instead. Who changed a setting is kept on the row only by Letta's archived server; GitHub and Slack keep it in a separate audit log.

### Per question

1. **Name.** Sources name a person's saved app-wide choices **settings**: the page is "Settings" in 4 of 4 sources with a UI, 9 of 9 GUIs checked and 9 of 9 wider products with a page, and "Preferences" is the page in none. The stored record is plural, `Settings` or `settings.json`, and the singular "setting" means one key; no product of 34 names a record type `Setting`. "Config" is the more common file or type name in the nine (6 of 9 against 4 of 9), but 4 of those 6 name configuration a developer writes in code, not choices saved through a UI.
2. **Shape.** The settings themselves are a typed document in 9 of 9 sources and 12 of 12 wider products. Where TypeScript agent GUIs persist settings in a database, 5 of 7 use a table with `key` and `value` columns, whose value is JSON: one row per key or section (Emdash, Crystal, CloudCLI, opcode) or one row holding the whole typed document (OpenCode). A singleton typed row (Superset) is the minority, and it shows the cost: 39 of 60 migrations touch it, against 1 of 47 for Emdash's key-value table.
3. **Layers.** 4 of 9 layer stored settings, and all 4 share user, project and managed or system layers, with the narrower layer winning and managed on top in 3 of 4. For a single-human local factory, the layer they all share that is about one person on one machine is **user** [Inferred]; the others serve repositories, organizations or one run.
4. **Fields.** A majority of the nine keep a default **model** (6 of 9, all named `model`), a **theme** (5 of 9, all named `theme`) and an **effort** (5 of 9, named differently). A default permission mode, notifications and telemetry are each kept by 4 of 9; the first two by a majority of the 13 GUIs (7 and 10), telemetry by 6 of 13; a harness choice by 0 of 9 but 8 of 13 GUIs; a bridge or terminal host by 2 of 9 (Claude Code's `teammateMode`). So the harness choice is backed by the GUIs (8 of 13), not by the nine, and the bridge choice by neither: only Claude Code's `teammateMode` (2 of 9, with the Agent SDK) and Emdash's `preferredConversationType` (1 of 13) come close.
5. **Metadata.** Settings files keep no `updatedAt`, no changed-by and, except Codex, no version; 4 of 9 carry `$schema`. Settings stored in database rows keep an update time in 11 of 13 products. Who changed a setting is kept on the row by 1 product of 34.
